title: Python Magic Methods and Operator Overloading
learningObjectives: Explain the core concepts of Python Magic Methods and Operator Overloading.
Choose an appropriate object-oriented design for a small Python problem.
Trace object state and method calls accurately.
Apply Python class features with correct method and attribute behavior.
Recognize design trade-offs, edge cases and maintainability concerns.

understand.concept: Special methods (often called magic or dunder methods) let user-defined objects participate in Python protocols. __str__ provides readable text, __repr__ provides a developer-oriented representation, __eq__ defines equality, __len__ supports len(), and arithmetic methods such as __add__ define supported operators. Implement only coherent behavior and follow each method's contract.
understand.whyItMatters: Special methods allow custom types to work naturally with built-in syntax and functions without inventing unrelated APIs.
understand.analogy: A standard plug fits a standard socket because both follow an agreed interface; special methods let custom objects follow Python's built-in protocols.
understand.summary: Python Magic Methods and Operator Overloading introduces a focused part of Python's object model and its practical use.

explain.narrative: Study the concept, trace the receiver and state for each operation, then run the examples. Pay attention to Python's conventions and documented protocol behavior rather than assuming that class syntax provides strict access control.

examples.title: Readable string with __str__
examples.code:
class Product:
    def __init__(self, name): self.name = name
    def __str__(self): return self.name
print(str(Product('Notebook')))
examples.explanation: str() calls __str__ for a user-facing representation.

examples.title: Developer representation with __repr__
examples.code:
class Point:
    def __init__(self, x, y): self.x, self.y = x, y
    def __repr__(self): return f'Point({self.x}, {self.y})'
print(repr(Point(2, 5)))
examples.explanation: repr() should ideally be unambiguous and useful for debugging.

examples.title: Define equality
examples.explanation: Returning NotImplemented for unsupported types lets Python try the reflected comparison.

examples.title: Support len()
examples.explanation: __len__ supplies the length protocol used by len().

practise.guidedTask: Build a small program that demonstrates python magic methods and operator overloading. Write down the object types, relevant attributes, method calls and expected state changes before running it.
practise.independentTask: Extend the example into a small domain model of your choice. Add validation, clear method names, boundary tests and a short explanation of why your design uses classes rather than simpler functions or data structures.

Use composition when it models the relationship more accurately than inheritance.
practise.challenge: Refactor the model into a testable design with clear responsibilities, documented public behavior and tests for normal, boundary and invalid cases.
validationCriteria: All five examples execute on the supported Python version and match their outputs.
The implementation follows Python's documented class and special-method semantics.
